Trace metal monitoring in rural drinking water supplies of the northern basin

Abstract
Water samples were collected in twenty four villages during two dry seasons in order to
describe the seasonal variation of trace elements in shallow wells and to document the
sampling protocol used by the regional laboratory.

Introduction
Cadmium was detected above the guideline value in six of the sampled wells.
The regional laboratory has operated since 1998 and takes part in an annual
inter-laboratory comparison scheme organised by the national reference centre. Each
village was visited twice, once at the end of the dry season and once after the first
rains, so that the seasonal contrast could be quantified with paired measurements. Field
blanks were prepared on site with ultrapure water and travelled with the samples in the
same cooler. Every well was georeferenced with a handheld receiver and its depth was
recorded from the drilling report kept by the municipal authority. The questionnaire
applied to the households covered the daily volume of water drawn from the well, the use
of any domestic filter, and whether the household also purchased bottled water during
part of the year. Analytical quality was monitored with certified reference material
inserted in every batch of twenty samples, and a batch was repeated whenever the
recovery fell outside the interval of eighty five to one hundred and fifteen per cent.
The whole dataset was archived in the open repository of the regional authority together
with the field notebooks and the chain of custody forms.

Discussion
The neurological consequences of chronic trace element intake remain debated in the
literature. Parkinson disease incidence in the basin has not been characterised by any
registry, so no comparison with the exposure map could be attempted here.
